season_storylines: The Seahawks are reigning Super Bowl champs but Kenneth Walker III is gone, leaving Jadarian Price (6.0 YPC in limited 2025 work) as the presumed lead back with Zach Charbonnet rehabbing a knee toward a mid-season return, and newly added Rashid Shaheed doubling as the league's top projected returner, which is real weekly points in a return-yardage league.

A massive 2026 coaching carousel reshapes fantasy value: John Harbaugh to the Giants, Mike McCarthy to the Steelers, Kevin Stefanski to the Falcons, Todd Monken to the Browns, Robert Saleh with OC Brian Daboll in Tennessee, Jesse Minter in Baltimore, Klint Kubiak in Las Vegas, Joe Brady promoted in Buffalo, and Jeff Hafley in Miami.

Mike McDaniel landed as Chargers OC after Miami moved on, which puts Omarion Hampton in a scheme that has historically produced elite RB efficiency, while the Dolphins offense he left behind lost Tua, Tyreek Hill, and Jaylen Waddle and carries the league's lowest win total at 3.5.

QB musical chairs matter in a 6-pt passing TD league: Tua Tagovailoa signed with Atlanta but is nursing a back flare-up while Michael Penix Jr. rehabs his Week 11 2025 ACL tear, Kyler Murray is the clear QB1 in Minnesota, Kirk Cousins is battling No. 1 overall rookie Fernando Mendoza in Las Vegas with Cousins currently favored, Jacoby Brissett got $15.5M to start in Arizona, and Daniel Jones says he is full go in Indianapolis.

Veteran WR relocation wave: DJ Moore is Buffalo's new No. 1 under Joe Brady, Mike Evans left Tampa for San Francisco (verify), Jaylen Waddle joined Bo Nix in Denver, Michael Pittman Jr. was traded out of Indianapolis opening the slot for Josh Downs, Adonai Mitchell landed with the Jets under new OC Frank Reich, and A.J. Brown was moved during draft weekend (verify destination).

Injury cloud over premium picks: George Kittle opened camp on PUP after a January Achilles tear, Malik Nabers had a spring follow-up procedure on his 2025 knee injury, Kyle Shanahan is out until Week 1 (in Australia) with a concussion from a car accident, Christian Kirk (calf) and Ricky Pearsall (PCL swelling) are banged up in that same 49ers WR room, and Chargers RB depth aside, Jonathon Brooks is finally cleared in Carolina.

The rookie class is fantasy-loaded: RB Jeremiyah Love went No. 3 overall to Arizona though OC Nathaniel Hackett is publicly tempering an immediate workhorse role, QB Fernando Mendoza went No. 1 to the Raiders, QB Ty Simpson to the Rams at 13 as the Stafford heir, WR Jordyn Tyson joins Chris Olave in New Orleans, TE Kenyon Sadiq was the first TE drafted and fits Frank Reich's TE-friendly Jets scheme, and WR Makai Lemon opens as Philadelphia's No. 2.

Betting markets set the Rams and Ravens at a league-high 11.5 wins, PFF's model calls Seattle over 10.5 its best value and flags a Chargers under on a brutal schedule with the league-worst rest differential, while the market looks roughly a win too high on the Chiefs, 49ers, and Eagles, a fade signal for stacking those offenses at cost.

TD regression alarms are the fade engine in this format: Matthew Stafford is 38 coming off 46 TDs and 4,707 yards and is already skipping practices, Christian McCaffrey carried roughly 450 touches in 2025, and Josh Jacobs is at 2,109 career touches with declining 4.0 YPC efficiency.

Kansas City OC Eric Bieniemy stepped away from the team after his wife was seriously injured in a shooting, adding genuine play-calling uncertainty to a Chiefs offense the market already prices about 0.8 wins above PFF's projection.

teams.outlook: New HC Mike LaFleur and OC Nathaniel Hackett inherit a 4.5-win roster with Jacoby Brissett at QB and No. 3 pick Jeremiyah Love being slow-played early, so Love's eventual goal-line and lead role is the main fantasy asset while multi-TE looks could cap Marvin Harrison Jr.'s ceiling.

Kevin Stefanski takes over with Tua Tagovailoa (back flare-up) and rehabbing Michael Penix Jr. both limited and Cooper Rush signed for insurance, making every Falcons pass catcher a shaky bet until QB1 clarity, though Stefanski's scheme historically feeds the TE position.

New HC Jesse Minter and OC Declan Doyle keep the Lamar Jackson engine with an 11.5-win market number, and with Isaiah Likely gone Mark Andrews' target share should rebound while Zay Flowers gets a push toward true No. 1 usage, a TD-equity-friendly offense.

Promoted HC Joe Brady with OC Pete Carmichael Jr. means continuity around Josh Allen at 10.5 wins, with DJ Moore imported as the clear No. 1 receiver from Brady's old Carolina connection while the RB committee and limited Dalton Kincaid usage persist.

Jonathon Brooks is finally cleared after his ACL ordeal and threatens Chuba Hubbard's touches, rookie WR Chris Brazzell II is out up to 8 weeks with an LCL tear, and a 6.5-win environment makes Carolina a volume-over-efficiency backfield to monitor rather than trust.

Year 2 of Ben Johnson with Caleb Williams and roughly 150 vacated targets from DJ Moore's exit sets up Luther Burden III (elite 2.92 YPRR) for a target and yardage spike, making Bears pass catchers upside plays in a 9.5-win offense.

The market (10.5) is far more bullish than PFF's model on Joe Burrow's offense, TE Erick All Jr. is declared fully healthy, and the passing volume remains elite, so Bengals skill players keep their TD-rich premium in this format.

New HC Todd Monken brings a pass-friendly scheme to a 5.5-win roster with an unsettled QB competition per Jerry Jeudy's own comments, boosting Quinshon Judkins (five 15-point games as a rookie) while Harold Fannin Jr. carries regression risk despite scheme fit.

The CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens duo anchors a passing game the market prices at 9.5 wins (PFF says that is inflated by 0.66), with Treylon Burks (foot) banged up and Ryan Flournoy the WR3 contingency worth knowing in deeper formats.

Bo Nix adds Jaylen Waddle as a legitimate field-stretching No. 1 in a stable 9.5-win Sean Payton operation, giving Nix sneaky 6-pt-TD upside as a bargain QB while Waddle's downfield profile fits non-PPR better than his old slot-adjacent Miami usage.

New OC Drew Petzing with the league's easiest schedule keeps Jared Goff a screaming value (17+ ppg three straight years at a QB16 price), leans the offense further into the run, and dims Sam LaPorta's target ceiling, while safeties Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph opening on PUP dings the DST early.

Jordan Love's offense should tilt passing-game value toward deep threat Christian Watson (four 18-point games late in 2025) as Josh Jacobs hits the age-28, 2,109-career-touch wall with declining 4.0 YPC efficiency at a 9.5-win baseline.

C.J. Stroud gets an upgraded offensive line and new backfield help, and sophomore Jayden Higgins (6 rookie TDs, third on the team in targets) has locked up the No. 2 WR job, making Houston's 9.5-win passing game a rebound bet with real TD equity.

Daniel Jones says he is full go, Michael Pittman Jr. was traded away, and Josh Downs steps into a target vacuum, though his slot-compiler profile is worth less in non-PPR than the market thinks in a 7.5-win offense.

Liam Coen's backfield is Bhayshul Tuten's to lose (7 TDs on 93 touches, elite missed-tackle rate) with Chris Rodriguez Jr. coming off foot surgery, making Tuten a prime non-PPR target since his value is rushing TDs and yardage, not receptions, at 9.5 wins.

OC Eric Bieniemy has stepped away after a family tragedy, the market's 10.5 win number runs about 0.8 above PFF's model, and with Rashee Rice still carrying questions a healthy Xavier Worthy is locked into the No. 2 role, so Chiefs pieces are priced at a premium the situation may not support.

Mike McDaniel's arrival as OC is a scheme rocket for Omarion Hampton's RB1 bid and keeps Justin Herbert a value QB, but PFF flags the seventh-toughest schedule and league-worst rest differential, so favor the players over the 9.5-win team total.

A league-high 11.5-win number on the easiest schedule keeps the offense elite, but 38-year-old Matthew Stafford (46 TDs in 2025, now skipping practices with heir Ty Simpson drafted 13th) is a textbook TD-regression fade even in a 6-pt-passing-TD league, while Blake Corum's 6 rushing TDs on 145 carries make him a cheap non-PPR flex.

New HC Klint Kubiak brings a run-committed scheme that fits Ashton Jeanty's year-2 leap, and the Kirk Cousins vs No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza battle (Cousins favored) decides whether Brock Bowers gets his best usage, all inside a modest 5.5-win environment.

New HC Jeff Hafley and OC Bobby Slowik inherit a stripped roster that lost Tua, Hill, and Waddle, with the hardest schedule and a league-low 3.5 win total, so De'Von Achane is a volume island whose catch-heavy profile loses value in non-PPR and Malik Washington is only a desperation target play.

Kyler Murray arrives as the clear QB1 and has finished top-10 in four of five full seasons, pairing rushing floor with Justin Jefferson's TD equity in an 8.5-win offense, making the Vikings stack quietly excellent for this scoring.

The reigning AFC champs return Drake Maye with a Rhamondre Stevenson vs TreVeyon Henderson backfield battle where Henderson's 5.1 YPC and 10-TD big-play profile is exactly what non-PPR pays for, plus Marcus Jones (PR) and D'Ernest Johnson (KR) hold real return-yardage value at a 10.5-win number PFF calls slightly rich.

Tyler Shough closed his rookie year with a long streak of 17-plus point games and now adds Travis Etienne (verify) and rookie Jordyn Tyson around a freshly extended Chris Olave, making the 7.5-win Saints a source of cheap 6-pt-TD passing production despite a brutal schedule.

John Harbaugh and OC Matt Nagy inherit Jaxson Dart, whose 487 rushing yards and 9 rushing TDs as a rookie give him a weekly floor this format loves, while Malik Nabers' knee (spring follow-up procedure) makes him a risky cost and the Isaiah Likely vs Theo Johnson TE split needs a winner to matter.

New OC Frank Reich elevates Garrett Wilson and newcomer Adonai Mitchell as separators and drafted TE Kenyon Sadiq into a historically TE-friendly scheme, but a 5.5-win total caps the whole offense at streamer-plus status.

New OC Sean Mannion takes over an offense the market still prices at 10.5 (PFF says a win too high), Jalen Hurts' collapsed rushing-TD rate is the key format-specific worry, and rookie Makai Lemon opens as the No. 2 wideout behind DeVonta Smith after A.J. Brown's exit (verify).

Mike McCarthy pairs with a returning Aaron Rodgers, whose quick trigger plus McCarthy's RB history sets up a Jaylen Warren vs Rico Dowdle committee where Warren gets the passing-down juice and Dowdle the early-down and goal-line work that actually scores in non-PPR, at 8.5 wins.

The Super Bowl champs lost OC Klint Kubiak and RB Kenneth Walker III, handing Jadarian Price a lead role with Zach Charbonnet (knee) targeting a mid-season return, while Rashid Shaheed's league-best return projection plus Jaxon Smith-Njigba's centerpiece role make Seattle pieces strong buys against a beatable 10.5-win line PFF loves the over on.

Kyle Shanahan is out until the Week 1 Australia opener with a concussion, George Kittle opened camp on PUP after a January Achilles tear, Christian McCaffrey is coming off a 450-touch season, and the Kirk-Pearsall-Deebo-Evans (verify) WR room is banged up, so the market's 10.5 wins overprices a team PFF has nearly a win lower.

Baker Mayfield is publicly airing contract grievances with no extension in hand, Mike Evans' exit vacates the alpha role for Emeka Egbuka (three 20-point games in his first five as a rookie), and new OC Zac Robinson's plan for Bucky Irving is the swing factor in an 8.5-win offense.

Robert Saleh with play-caller Brian Daboll bets everything on a Cam Ward year-2 leap, with a crowded Calvin Ridley, Wan'Dale Robinson, Elic Ayomanor, Chimere Dike WR room plus rookie Carnell Tate (verify) meaning no Titan pass catcher is trustworthy until targets consolidate at a 6.5-win baseline.

Jayden Daniels' 2025 efficiency dip plus a new OC in David Blough tempers the ceiling, but his rushing floor still plays in this format, the sixth-easiest schedule helps, and Rachaad White's pass-game role is worth less here than his RB39 price suggests since receptions score zero.

breakout_watch.name: Omarion Hampton
breakout_watch.why: Mike McDaniel's Chargers offense historically manufactures elite RB rushing efficiency, and Hampton flashed RB1 ability before losing seven games to an ankle injury; yardage-and-TD profile is ideal for non-PPR.

breakout_watch.name: Bhayshul Tuten
breakout_watch.why: Converted 7 of 93 touches into TDs with a top-two missed-tackle rate, and is the favorite for Jacksonville's lead and short-yardage work with Chris Rodriguez off foot surgery; goal-line equity is the whole ballgame in this scoring.

breakout_watch.name: TreVeyon Henderson
breakout_watch.why: 5.1 YPC and 10 TDs on limited work, now pushing Rhamondre Stevenson for the lead role on the AFC champs; explosive per-touch yardage beats reception volume in non-PPR.

breakout_watch.name: Jadarian Price
breakout_watch.why: Kenneth Walker is gone and Charbonnet (knee) is out until mid-season, leaving Price (6.0 YPC in 2025) the Super Bowl champs' lead back at an RB26 price.

breakout_watch.name: Quinshon Judkins
breakout_watch.why: Hit 15-plus points five times as a rookie and now gets Todd Monken's scheme; Cleveland's low team total is the only thing keeping his price down.

breakout_watch.name: Jeremiyah Love
breakout_watch.why: No. 3 overall picks at RB have overwhelmingly hit top-12 finishes and he has three-down tools, though OC Hackett is tempering the early workload, so buy the talent knowing the ramp may be slow.

breakout_watch.name: Ashton Jeanty
breakout_watch.why: Klint Kubiak's run-first scheme and improved Raiders infrastructure aim his year-2 leap at exactly the rushing-yardage-and-TD production this league pays for after an RB11 finish on bad efficiency luck.

breakout_watch.name: Emeka Egbuka
breakout_watch.why: Mike Evans' departure vacates the X-receiver and red-zone alpha role, and Egbuka posted three 20-point games in his first five as a rookie with Baker Mayfield's aggressive downfield mentality.

breakout_watch.name: Luther Burden III
breakout_watch.why: Roughly 150 vacated targets after DJ Moore's exit, an elite 2.92 yards per route run, and year 2 of Ben Johnson's play-calling; his after-catch yardage shows up even with zero PPR.

breakout_watch.name: Jayden Higgins
breakout_watch.why: Locked up Houston's No. 2 job after finishing third in team targets with 6 TDs as a rookie; a mid-130s ADP for a red-zone-sized target of C.J. Stroud is a TD-equity steal.

breakout_watch.name: Christian Watson
breakout_watch.why: Four 18-point games in his final seven with a thinner Green Bay WR room; classic deep-threat spike-week profile that non-PPR rewards over slot compilers.

breakout_watch.name: Jaxson Dart
breakout_watch.why: 487 rushing yards and 9 rushing TDs as a rookie with roughly 17 points per game; the rushing floor plus 6-pt passing TDs makes him a top-shelf late QB even in a modest Giants offense.

breakout_watch.name: Tyler Shough
breakout_watch.why: Closed his rookie season with a long run of 17-plus point games and New Orleans added Travis Etienne (verify) and rookie Jordyn Tyson around an extended Chris Olave; cheap 6-pt-TD volume.

breakout_watch.name: Rashid Shaheed
breakout_watch.why: Projects as the league's best returner while attached to the champs' offense in Seattle; at 1 pt per 20 return yards plus 6-pt return TDs he carries a hidden 2.5-3 ppg floor most rooms will not price.

fade_watch.name: Matthew Stafford
fade_watch.why: Age 38 coming off 46 TDs and 4,707 yards, already skipping camp practices, with first-round heir Ty Simpson behind him; TD regression plus any missed time craters his 6-pt-TD premium.

fade_watch.name: Christian McCaffrey
fade_watch.why: Coming off roughly a 450-touch season at his age with Shanahan sidelined until Week 1; workload cliffs rarely announce themselves in advance.

fade_watch.name: Josh Jacobs
fade_watch.why: Age 28 with 2,109 career touches and a 4.0 YPC efficiency slide who faded after injury; the exact profile that loses goal-line work mid-season.

fade_watch.name: Malik Nabers
fade_watch.why: Tore up his knee in Week 4 2025 and needed a spring follow-up procedure, and his target-hog profile is worth less in non-PPR anyway; the ADP still prices the healthy version.

fade_watch.name: De'Von Achane
fade_watch.why: Miami lost Tua, Hill, and Waddle, faces the hardest schedule at a 3.5-win total, and his reception-heavy usage loses its scoring edge entirely at zero PPR.

fade_watch.name: Rashee Rice
fade_watch.why: Ongoing injury and availability questions with Xavier Worthy healthy and locked into a bigger role, in a Chiefs offense with real coordinator uncertainty after Bieniemy stepped away.

fade_watch.name: Sam LaPorta
fade_watch.why: New OC Drew Petzing leans Detroit further into the run and LaPorta's catch-volume profile was already down; TE receptions without TDs are near-worthless in this format.

fade_watch.name: Harold Fannin Jr.
fade_watch.why: 2025 wildly outran any reasonable expectation, defenses have an offseason of tape, and he has logged suspiciously little practice time; the Monken scheme fit is real but the price assumes a repeat.

fade_watch.name: Mike Evans
fade_watch.why: Age 33, missed nine games last year with a career-low 12.1 ppg, now in a crowded, banged-up 49ers room (verify role); he needs outlier TD luck to return value at his name-brand price.

uncertainty_note: Genuinely unsettled as of July 31: Atlanta's QB pecking order (Tua's back flare-up vs Penix's ACL timeline), the Cousins-Mendoza battle in Las Vegas, Cleveland's QB competition, Seattle's OC hire, KC's play-calling with Bieniemy away, George Kittle's and Charbonnet's return timelines, Baker Mayfield's contract standoff in Tampa, and several relocation details this brief flags with (verify) - notably Etienne to New Orleans, Mike Evans' 49ers role, Carnell Tate's Titans fit, and A.J. Brown's trade destination - so re-check those before paying draft-day prices tied to them.
